research.name: Self-test: planted pattern
research.description: Fades a sweep of the previous UTC day's high or low: when price pokes above yesterday's high and closes back below it, go short (mirror for the low). Stop just beyond the sweep, target 1R, exit after 16 bars.
research.demo_note: A pattern was planted in the synthetic CTRL-SYN prices on purpose. If the gate could not find it, the gate would be broken. It proves the test works — it is never a trading idea.

checks.name: Beats random entries (never-seen months)
checks.value: p = 0.001 · random entries win 47.0%, -0.06R per trade

checks.name: Beats random entries (last 3 months)
checks.value: p = 0.001 · random entries win 46.9%, -0.06R per trade

reasons: Wins 86.2% of trades in the never-seen months (95% CI 75%-93%) and 86.4% in the last 3 months, making +0.68R per trade after costs.
Random entries with the same stop and target win only 47.0% (p = 0.001).
Passing this test is not permission to trade: next comes a 30-40 trade forward test at minimum lot on your broker's data.

research.stage_note: Qualified, but it is the self-test on synthetic data — never traded.

research.name: Sweep Fade (demo)

research.demo_note: The demo prices for real-named symbols contain no edge at all. This rule should look like random entries — and it does. That is the honest result.

report.title: Daily report — 2026-11-02
report.markdown:
# Daily report — 2026-11-02

**Data:** synthetic demo set (7 symbols, M15, 24 months to 2026-10-30). The numbers show how the system works, not real performance.

## Verdict

- **1 of 6** agents passed the 80% gate: the planted-pattern self-test, which proves the gate can detect a real pattern.
- **0** signals are eligible for money. Demo data is never eligible.
- Kill switch is **off**. No trades were placed — v1 cannot place trades.

## Agents on never-seen months

| Agent | Wins | Hit full stop | Profit per trade | Better than random? | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Self-test: planted pattern | 86% | 12% | +0.68R | Yes (p = 0.001) | Qualified |
| Sweep Fade (demo) | 51% | 45% | −0.02R | No (p = 0.45) | Failed |
| Range Breakout (demo) | 48% | 35% | 0.00R | No (p = 0.47) | Failed |
| Trend Pullback (demo) | 57% | 36% | +0.27R | No (p = 0.11) | Too few trades |
| Tight Target (trap demo) | 81% | 18% | −0.04R | No (p = 0.48) | Failed |
| Leaky Rule (demo) | 92% | 8% | +0.78R | Yes (p = 0.001) | Blocked |

## What the supervisor caught

1. `leaky` reads the next bar's close. The leak check blocked it.
2. `tight_target` wins about 80% of trades but loses money: random entries win just as often.
3. `trend_pullback` is too strict: too few trades to judge.

## Next steps

- Export broker data with `tools/export_mt5_data.py` on the Windows PC and run again on that data.
- Review the pending change **chg-002**. Nothing changes without your YES.
- An agent that qualifies on broker data starts a forward test: *30–40 trades at minimum lot*.

> Agents don't create an edge; they only test ideas faster. Simple fixed rules, proven small first.
